Eleven rules in `pricebook.py` didn't match their docstrings. I fixed all of them, and now every one of the 150 rules matches its docstring. I checked this with a script that builds the expected result from each docstring and the module's shared rules. It compared against the code for quantities 0–299, 1000 and 5000, at 7 unit prices each. Before the fix it flagged exactly these 11 rules; after the fix it flags none.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 19, 40 | Discount started at 11 units instead of 10 | Threshold `>= 10` |
| 21, 52, 144 | The 30,000 won cap was applied to the price before taking the percentage, not to the discount | Calculate the discount, then cap it |
| 51, 53 | Discount was rounded with `round()`, which can round up | Round down to the won (`//`) |
| 74 | Rule is "whole" but only discounted units above 12 | Discount the whole amount |
| 118 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won | Always cap at 30,000 won |
| 136, 145 | Rule is "marginal" but discounted the whole amount | Discount only units above the threshold |

Rule 67 starts at `qty >= 31` instead of 30. At exactly 30 units its discount is 0 either way, so the result is the same and I left it unchanged.

STATUS: DONE
